subject: Private VPC — operator witnessing alternative & limited escrow proposal
messages:
From: Jessica Lai <jessica.lai@finserv.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finserv.com
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC — operator witnessing alternative to escrow request

David,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and our legal team are aligned on the need for stronger evidence and operator controls for any private VPC deployment. We do not want to request a full code escrow, but we need a defensible alternative that gives us the ability to verify continuity in the event of a material provider failure.

High-level asks from legal/procurement:
- Written operator exhibit that limits Redwood operator rights, includes runbook witness steps.
- Periodic sealed snapshot deposit or third-party witness session to prove access capabilities.
- A short list of evidence items (runbooks, access logs, operator attestation) and how often they can be delivered.

Can you share a proposal or redline language we can take to counsel? Procurement would like to include this in the Order Form schedule for the pilot.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our procurement window is ~2 weeks.

--
Jessica Lai
Senior Procurement Manager
FinServ Bank

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Lai <jessica.lai@finserv.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC — operator witnessing alternative to escrow request

Jessica — thanks for the clear outline. Looping in Lauren (legal) and Tessa (product/ops) to scope a pragmatic path. Initial thoughts from my side:

- We can offer a two-track approach: (A) Witness-lite: periodic remote witnessed runbook execution + sealed snapshot deposits (encrypted, time-stamped) retained by a mutually agreed custodian; (B) Auditor-backed attestations: quarterly third-party attestation of operator procedures and a standing remote witness window.
- Both avoid full escrow of source code or binaries; instead preserve verifiability of operator capability and data access flows.
- We will put proposed MSA/Order Form exhibit language in a redline and surface the minimal indemnities/SLAs this impacts.

I attached the initial exhibit draft and an evidence matrix stub. Also adding our HubSpot deal id for reference (HS-98321) and a DocuSign envelope placeholder once counsel signs off.

Attachments: VPC_Operator_Exhibit_v1.docx, evidence-matrix.xlsx

Next steps: Lauren — can you propose guarded language we can share with FinServ counsel? Tessa — can you confirm operational feasibility/scheduling for witness windows?

Thanks,
David

--
David Kim
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Jessica Lai <jessica.lai@finserv.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC — operator witnessing alternative to escrow request

Jessica, David — reviewed the ask and sketched contract language to keep this procurement-friendly while protecting Redwood IP and operational security. Key legal positions:

- Replace any blanket "escrow" requirement with a defined "Operator Evidence Exhibit" that describes deliverables and conditions (sealed snapshot, witness sessions, runbook excerpts).
- Limit the scope of disclosed materials to operational runbooks and evidence artifacts only; exclude source code and model weights.
- Time-boxed access: remote, recorded witness sessions or delivery of encrypted snapshots to a neutral custodian under defined triggers (e.g., bankruptcy, material breach, takeover).
- Use a narrow proof-of-access test (not full system handoff) to validate continuity.
- Add an assurance clause requiring Redwood to maintain SOC 2 Type II and provide quarterly summary attestations tied to the exhibit.

I've attached a redline of the exhibit with placeholders for the cadence and custodian details (VPC_Operator_Exhibit_v2_redline.docx). Operational items for Tessa: please confirm the effort to schedule a 2-hour remote witness session quarterly and what logs/artifacts we can reasonably produce without exposing sensitive internals.

Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Procurement Team <procurement@finserv.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC — operator witnessing alternative to escrow request

Thanks for the draft language, Lauren. Counsels' feedback: they like the Operator Evidence Exhibit concept but want to preserve the ability to request an on-site witness for the pilot if remote sessions prove insufficient. They also asked whether Redwood would accept a narrowly scoped indemnity extension tied to the exhibit for a limited period (pilot + 6 months).

Attached: FinServ_witness_requirements.pdf — this is the procurement team's baseline for witness activities and evidence delivery SLAs. Questions for Redwood:
- Can you confirm the maximum notice Redwood would need to stand up an on-site witness (if requested)?
- Would Redwood accept a short-term indemnity limited to demonstrable operator negligence during witness activities?
- If we proceed with sealed snapshots held by a custodian, can you propose acceptable custodians (or do you prefer a named neutral firm)?

Please let us know; procurement would like a shortlist by EOW so we can prep counsel redlines.

Best,
FinServ Procurement

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@finserv.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC — operator witnessing alternative to escrow request

Team — consolidating next steps and two pragmatic options for procurement to pick from this week: 

Option 1 — Witness-lite (recommended for pilot)
- Quarterly 2-hour remote witnessed runbook execution (screen shared, recorded).
- Sealed encrypted snapshot delivered to a neutral custodian (e.g., IronClad Custody, ThirdParty Audit Services) every 6 months; custodian holds snapshot sealed unless trigger met.
- Redwood provides quarterly SOC 2 summary attestations and access logs for witness sessions.
- Redwood declines broad indemnity; will accept a narrowly scoped indemnity covering operator negligence during scheduled witness activities (pilot + 6 months).

Option 2 — Auditor-backed attestation + on-site fallback
- Quarterly third-party attestation of operator procedures (Alex Gates from ThirdPartyAudit can perform).
- Standby on-site witness within 4 weeks' notice for the pilot phase if remote evidence is materially insufficient.
- Stronger evidence bundle but still no source-code escrow.

What I need from FinServ this week: pick a preferred option and confirm custody preference (we can provide a short list of custodians). Once we have that, Lauren will produce an MSA/Order Form exhibit redline for counterparty counsel and I will prepare the operations runbook template and timeline.

Attachments: VPC_Operator_Exhibit_v2_redline.docx, FinServ_witness_requirements.pdf

Thanks,
David

--

Redwood Inference
